svg.title: STR-001 Structural Notes & Design Criteria
svg.text: SHAMANDEEL, QUESNA, MENOUFIA, EGYPT · ECP 201 — Egyptian Code for Loads · ECP 203 — Egyptian Code for Reinforced Concrete
The frame set out: a grid, twelve column coordinates, six slab outlines, the spans between them
and the lines where a beam is required. All of it falls out of the architecture and all of it is
It exists so the structural engineer starts from a coordinated layout rather than from nothing,
and so the architecture cannot quietly move underneath the structure.
It is not a structural design. No member size, no slab or footing depth, no reinforcement, no
cover, no load and no analysis appears anywhere in it.
Design criteria — dead and imposed loads, wind, the seismic zone and its design ground
acceleration — are set and signed by the structural engineer to ECP 201, and the concrete to ECP
203. ECP 201 has five seismic zones; which governs Shamandeel is named by the engineer, not
GEO-001, the soil investigation. The ground is central Nile Delta and well characterised as a
region, which is enough to assume a foundation type and lay it out, and not enough to size one.
Allowable bearing pressure, the water table and sulphate content are plot figures.
SUR-001, the measured survey, for the boundary STR-400 sits on.
THE ONE RULE THE ARCHITECTURE ALREADY SETTLED
A 300 mm wall needs a beam under it, and a beam is a column line, a wall below, or a secondary
beam landing on primary beams. Every 300 mm wall in this building stands on a grid line, with
one exception: the penthouse's north wall, which is a line load on the +13.20 slab spanning B to
C. STR-305 carries a secondary beam under it for that reason.
The 100 mm partitions do not stand on grid lines and do not need to; they are carried by the
